horizontal.name: kill-switch-status-nosig
horizontal._comment: 2026-08-02: was expected_status 200. That assertion was written from what the route did, and the route's own comment then cited this surface ('a CI smoke surface calls it unauthenticated by design') as the reason the GET could stay public — a loop in which the test justified the code and the code justified the test, with no requirement anywhere. Observed live returning 200 to an anonymous caller with a body proving it had reached upstream, which it does with a borrowed PI_CEO_PASSWORD. The decision: an anonymous caller may not read swarm state through a credential it does not hold, so the GET now authenticates like the POST and this surface asserts the refusal. Keeping the dashboard console clean is not a reason to answer strangers.

horizontal.name: mesh-claim-self-nosig
horizontal._comment: UNI-2248 (PR #509): idle-runner atomic self-claim of the top-priority unclaimed mesh:auto ticket (app/server/routes/mesh.py claim_self). Requires X-Pi-CEO-Secret; unauthenticated POST returns 401 before any Linear query or mesh_work_claims insert, so this probe proves route + auth without ever creating a real claim. Same pattern as cost-report-nosig/margot-turn-nosig. An authenticated probe is deliberately NOT declared — a valid secret would self-claim a live ticket (state mutation); the claim race/priority logic is covered offline by tests/test_mesh_runner_idle_autoclaim.py.

horizontal.name: mesh-claims-reap-nosig
horizontal._comment: UNI-2301: stale-claim reaper (app/server/routes/mesh.py reap_claims) — releases mesh_work_claims rows stuck in claimed/working past MESH_CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES when the claiming machine's heartbeat is itself stale or absent, so a runner dying mid-claim can't lock a ticket forever. Requires X-Pi-CEO-Secret; unauthenticated POST returns 401 before any Supabase read or Linear mutation, same pattern as mesh-claim-self-nosig. An authenticated probe is deliberately NOT declared — a valid secret would run a real sweep against live claims (state mutation); the TTL/heartbeat/reclaim logic is covered offline by tests/test_mesh_claim_reap.py. UNI-2303 hardened reap internals (return=representation, hot-path isolation, TTL floor, released-reversal); NO endpoints added/removed — this existing 401 probe still covers the surface.

horizontal.name: mesh-heartbeat-nosig
horizontal._comment: PR #542: heartbeat upsert fixed to target the (machine, runtime, session_id) UNIQUE constraint via on_conflict — merge-duplicates alone resolved against the uuid PK and every repeat heartbeat 409'd (~8.6k/day, the bulk of the Supabase failure rate). Requires X-Pi-CEO-Secret; unauthenticated POST with a valid minimal body returns 401 inside the handler before any Supabase write, same pattern as mesh-claim-self-nosig. An authenticated probe is deliberately NOT declared — a valid secret would upsert a phantom 'smoke' machine row (state mutation); upsert semantics are asserted post-merge by watching mesh_agents POSTs return 2xx not 409 in the Supabase API logs.

horizontal.name: fable-canary
horizontal._comment: RA-1099 Wave-3: Fable adversary-canary amplification summary; require_auth so unauth=401. auth:false so the runner probes it BEFORE login with an empty cookie jar — require_auth then returns 401. (auth:true would run it post-login; the session cookie satisfies require_auth → 200, which is why RA-7028's first pass still failed 200!=401.) Backend route is /api/canary/fable on Railway; the e2e runner targets the Vercel base, so the surface must carry the /api/pi-ceo proxy prefix like every other backend surface (bare /api/canary/fable 404s at Vercel). The standalone .github/workflows/fable_canary_check.yml hits Railway directly and keeps the unprefixed path.

Bodies are ignored on 401. Reached through the dashboard /api/pi-ceo proxy prefix like every other FastAPI surface.
